prose: The Washington Sun reports from a pro-data-center party at PubKey, a cryptocurrency-themed bar in downtown DC: hundreds attended (a thousand RSVP'd) for a celebration of AI infrastructure, with themed cocktails - a peach-forward 'Loudoun County Iced Tea' nodding to Virginia's data center alley, an 'SMR-tini' espresso martini, and a 'Closed Loop Spritz' that sold out. The party was explicitly defensive, counterprogramming what the invite called a 'bipartisan psychosis' over data centers - at a moment when polls show three-quarters of Americans oppose local data center construction.

The organizers are three men from libertarian and conservative spaces: Jonas Du of Pirate Wires (Mike Solana's media company), Ed Tarnowski of the R Street Institute, and Casey Given of Young Voices. Industry speakers, including Build American AI's Nathan Leamer leading a pro-infrastructure chant, focused on beating China, conquering 'fear of the unknown,' and AI's world-transforming potential - while outside, communities fight data center construction tooth and nail.
highlights: Hundreds partied for data centers at PubKey in DC; 1,000 RSVP'd
Themed drinks: 'Loudoun County Iced Tea', 'SMR-tini', 'Closed Loop Spritz'
Explicit counterprogramming against what the invite called 'bipartisan psychosis' on data centers
Context: polls show ~75% of Americans oppose local data centers
Organizers: Pirate Wires' Jonas Du, R Street's Ed Tarnowski, Young Voices' Casey Given
Speaker themes: beating China, 'fear of the unknown', AI as world-transforming
